entries.test: Public statements and research by Marcus, Sutskever, Sutton, and hundreds of other researchers would establish whether they expressed serious doubts about LLMs by publication.
entries.note: Publicly expressed doubts provide a plain test without requiring access to private beliefs.
“I doubt” expresses a probabilistic assessment of success.

The proposition drops “I don’t think” and replaces the alleged ego-related mental block with rejection of symbolic AI. The claim concerns LeCun’s private understanding and its psychological explanation.

entries.test: Published architectures and formal-reasoning demonstrations could test whether successful world models require the specified explicit, structured, directly retrievable knowledge.
entries.note: The normalized proposition omits “if my 2020 article is correct,” although the separate conditions field preserves it.

entries.test: Public architecture documentation and controlled hallucination evaluations could test whether avoiding hallucinations requires explicit, structured world knowledge.
entries.note: This asserts a necessary technical condition, rather than merely recommending an approach.

entries.test: Public demonstrations of reliable AI systems, together with their architectures, could test whether trustworthy performance requires both neural and symbolic contributions.
entries.note: The claim asserts technical necessity; “my own view” does not make it an ought or merely a value judgment.

entries.test: Published JEPA architectures, interpretability analyses, and reasoning evaluations would test the claimed opacity and limitations for reasoning.
entries.note: The wording permits a shared technical reading despite lacking numerical thresholds.

entries.test: Public evaluations of JEPA-based systems against established LLM failure modes would show whether the approach solves many of those problems.
entries.note: “I don’t expect” states a firm negative expectation, with no deadline.

entries.test: Meta’s public JEPA project history, contributor records, publications, and released systems would establish the duration, team scale, and extent of its output by publication.
entries.note: The proposition removes “what appears to be” and the academic comparison for team size. The factual output claim is checkable even though “earth-shaking” is evaluative.
This is an evaluative verdict about need and adequacy without a specified success criterion.

entries.test: JEPA’s published architecture and evaluations of perception, structured representation, and world prediction would test the asserted capabilities and missing structure.
entries.note: The supporting words are Denis O’s quotation, explicitly endorsed by Marcus. Marcus supplies the final conclusion in his own voice.

entries.test: If the described credit-denial behavior occurs at the company, public employee accounts, workplace reporting, and morale surveys would test whether morale becomes very low.
entries.note: “Deathly low” has a plain reading as very low morale; the antecedent and outcome have no deadline.
Marcus endorses exploration of genuinely new approaches, but does not explicitly restrict that recommendation to approaches beyond LLMs. The claim about what the field needs is normative.
